title: Build and test on every change
summary: The CI job: triggers, permissions, and restore-build-test for the Orders API.

steps.title: The project
body: You maintain the **Orders API**, an ASP.NET Core app in `src/Api` with tests in `tests/Api.Tests` and a `Dockerfile` at the root.
Over four stages you will write its complete pipeline, `.github/workflows/api.yml`:
stage 1  build ─ test                         (every push and PR)
stage 2  + cache, test report, api artifact
stage 3  + image ─► ghcr.io                    (pushed only from main)
The workflow is written inside a C# raw string literal (`"""` ... `"""`) and printed, so the checks can read it.

steps.prompt: Pull requests from feature branches into `main` should be checked, and pushes to `main` should be checked too. Which `on` block does that?
steps.explain: `pull_request.branches` filters on the **target** branch of the PR, so `[main]` means "PRs into main".
Each `--no-...` flag reuses the work of the previous step and makes sure tests run against the exact build.

steps.title: Write the CI workflow
prompt: Replace the TODOs to produce a workflow that:
- is named `api` and runs on `push` and `pull_request` to `main`,
- has a job `build` on `ubuntu-latest` with the steps checkout (`actions/checkout@v7`), `actions/setup-dotnet@v6` with `dotnet-version: '10.0.x'`,
`dotnet restore`, `dotnet build --no-restore -c Release` and `dotnet test --no-build -c Release`.
The program prints your workflow file. **Run checks** runs it and looks for the required lines in the output. Indentation is YAML structure, so keep it consistent (two spaces per level).
